terms.comment: A country takes a preposition: in Ucraīnam (to), in Ucraīnā (in), ex Ucraīnā (from).

evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v. Bucovetia: Bucovetia, d. Ukraine, Lschf., Rußland; eh. d. Woiwodschaften Kijew u. Brailaw, Polen
terms.comment: Graesse’s name for the Ukraine of his day, the land around Kyiv. A country takes a preposition: in Bucovetiam, in Bucovetiā.

ucraina.html: The long vowel puts the Latin stress where Ukrainian Україна has it, by the convention for modern names.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio, geographical section, with the authorities it cites (cited as M-O s.v.).

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus, edition of F. Benedict (1909), Latin–German, read in the digitization at columbia.edu (cited as Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v.); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
